Yenamala Utta Reddy, ...PETITIONER  AND The State Of Andhra Pradesh and Others ...RESPONDENT(S)
Counsel for the Petitioner:
1. D SESHASAYANA REDDY

Counsel for the Respondent(S):
1. GP FOR MUNCIPAL ADMN URBAN DEV 2. S S BHATT 3. N RANGA REDDY (SC MC RSEEMA SPSR NLR)

The Court made the following ORDER :
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the respondent Nos.2 & 3 and the learned counsel for the respondent Nos.4 & 5.
2.

This writ petition is filed questioning the action of the respondent Nos.2 and 3 in taking appropriate steps to remove the illegal constructions made by the respondent Nos.4 and 5 in open site in Sy.No.447 in an extent of Ac.0.91 cents situated at B.K.Palli Village, Madanapalli Municipality Yenamala Utta Reddy, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8459757/
1 area, Annamaiah District, without having valid construction permit.
3.

sentences.text:
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that without obtaining valid permission from the respondent Nos.2 and 3, the 4 th respondent proceeded with the unauthorized construction by raising zinc sheets shed in the subject land i.e., Ac.0.91 cents situated at B.K.Palli Village,
Madanapalli Municipality area, Annamaiah District, within the limits of the 2 nd respondent.

4. On the other hand, the learned Standing Counsel relying upon the counter of the 2nd respondent s u b m i t s t h a t a l r e a d y t h e 2 n d r e s p o n d e n t i s s u e d a p r o v i s i o n a l n o t i c e v i d e U.C.B.A.No.02/Sec02/2023, dated 04.10.2023 under Section 228(1) & (2) of APM Act, 1965 to the 4 th respondent calling for submission of his explanation.

Later, the 2 nd respondent issued Confirmation Order vide Notice No.97/1009/MDP/UC/2023, dated 28.10.2023 under Section 228(3) & 340 of APM Act, 1965 and thus his office initiated steps as per the AP Municipalities Act,
1965 against the respondent Nos.4, 5 and the other.

The respondent Nos.4 & 5 submitted reply notice to the confirmation order issued by the 2nd respondent stating that they are in the possession and enjoyment of the subject land for the last so many years, having right and title over the subject land and raised temporary zinc sheets shed without any walls, which is purely temporary in nature.

5. In view of the interim orders granted by this Court, the 2nd respondent directed the respondent Nos.4 & 5, not to proceed with the construction vide ROC.No.02/Sec-02/2023, dated 12.12.2023 and accordingly they stopped the construction.
There are civil suits pending between the petitioners and the unofficial respondents in O.S.No.155 of 2006, O.S.No.39 of 2012 and the Land Acquisition Petition L.A.O.P.No.47 of 2000.

In addition to it, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent Nos.4 & 5 submits that the unofficial respondents are the absolute owners of the subject land having their title under the registered sale deed dated 05.04.1958.

Thereafter, the subject land in Sy.Nos.447/1 and 442/1 to an extent of Ac.1.85 cents and Ac.6.09 cents was conveyed through a fresh registered sale deed dated 16.09.1974, in favour of the father of the respondent Nos.4 & 5.
Under the land acquisition proceedings also, the father and the mother of the respondent Nos.4 & 5 have lost some portion of the subject land for which they were paid compensation.
The respondent Nos.4 & 5 approached the 2nd respondent seeking permission to raise temporary zinc sheets shed by submitting the letter dated 03.03.2023.
Since there was no action taken on the said representation, the unofficial respondents got issued legal notice.
In view of the interim directions of this Hon'ble Court dated 29.11.2023, the respondent Nos.4 & 5 did not proceed with any further construction.

6. In view of the above said facts and circumstances, it is to be seen that admittedly, the subject matter of the writ petition is also the subject matter in the above mentioned suits pending for consideration before the appropriate civil Courts, wherein, the unofficial respondents and the petitioner are the parties to the said proceedings who are contesting the matters on merits.
Subject to the outcome of the same, the petitioner as well as the unofficial respondents can approach the respondent Nos.2 and 3 with appropriate applications or representations.
Since the rights of the parties have to be determined in the above said civil suits, the pendency of this writ petition is not warranted and accordingly it is liable to be dismissed.
However, the liberty is given to the parties to work out their remedies otherwise in accordance with law.
